objective: Give every game a page of its own at /games/:gameId, built from GET /events/games/{id}: the two teams and the final score, the line score and the full box score of each team; and make games clickable wherever the app shows one, so a reader can open any game.
acceptance_criteria: /games/:gameId is a public route under AppLayout that fetches GET /events/games/{gameId} and renders a level-one heading naming both teams (away at home, by name) with the final score, the game's date, its label and sub-label when present (for example NBA Finals, Game 5) and its venue when present.
The winning team is marked in text or with an icon carrying an accessible name, never by colour alone.

When both teams have a line score, the page renders it as a table with a caption, a row per team and a column per period headed Q1-Q4, then OT, 2OT and 3OT+ for the fifth, sixth and seventh figures, then the total; when either is null the table is absent and nothing else changes.

Each team's box score is a table with a caption naming the team, a header row with scope=col headers (Player, MIN, FG, 3P, FT, FG%, 3P%, FT%, OREB, DREB, REB, AST, STL, BLK, TO, PF, +/-, PTS), the starters first, then the bench, in the order the API returns them, a totals row, and minutes shown as m:ss from seconds_played; percentages from the API show as a three-place decimal without a leading zero (.462), and a null percentage shows as an en dash.
Players who did not play are listed under each team's table with their reason, or 'Did not play' when the reason is null.
A game with empty box scores renders the heading and line score and, in place of each table, an explicit empty state saying no box score is available.
An unknown game id renders a not-found message with a link back to the feed; any other failure renders an InlineAlert; neither throws.
The box-score tables scroll horizontally inside their own container at a 360 px viewport, and the page itself never scrolls horizontally.
GameScore accepts an optional link target, and every GameScore the app renders (the search page's game results) links to that game's page.

In a post's text, every #GameId<n> token whose n is in the post's mentioned_game_ids renders as a link to /games/<n> with the token as its text; a token that is not in mentioned_game_ids stays plain text; the post text is never parsed as HTML.

Every *.module.css file this unit adds or changes contains no hex, rgb(), hsl() or named colour, no px font size, and no outline: none or outline: 0 without a :focus-visible rule in the same file (a static test reads the files from disk).

Every link on the page and each box-score scroll container is reachable with Tab and shows a visible focus ring, and the PR carries the browser checklist of FrontendUI/verification.md for /games/:gameId (light and dark, 360 and 1280 wide), with the axe row left to the human.
